On KV cache: between cold storage (HDD) and the running application (NAND) sits a warm-storage tier with several sub-tiers, and 'for sure there are some tiers inside KV cache that can use hard disk drive' - the only place where NAND and HDD overlap. Seagate does not need a flash partner for it, only to meet the performance requirement of the relevant tier. On neoclouds: today they run compute against storage that physically sits in the public cloud, so Seagate sells the same drives to the same public-cloud customers; if neoclouds start serving their own customers they 'cannot access the public cloud storage anymore' and will need their own storage, shifting some of that volume directly to neoclouds - positive for customer diversification, roughly neutral on volume.
